 BMW's Latest Water Pump Fire Recall Covers 720,000 Vehicles and Comes With a "Park Outside" Advisory
 NHTSA and BMW of North America warn that affected models could catch fire even while switched off and parked, hence the "park outside" warning 
 Published: 16 Nov 2026, 08:43 UTC 
 By: 
 Mircea Panait 
   9 photos Photo: BMW 
 BMW is recalling a massive 720,796 vehicles in the United States market for water pump connectors that may short circuit, increasing the risk of a fire. Even though lab tests found embrittlement and cracks in the electrical connector's material, the Bavarian automaker still hasn't identified the root cause. 
 26V733 is what the federal watchdog calls this campaign, which also comes with a "park outside" advisory due to the fire risk. Customers are urged to park away from buildings and other vehicles until dealers complete the repair.
 This recall started with an older campaign, specifically 24V608 from August 2024. Back in April 2025, the German manufacturer learned of a thermal overload incident at the water pump connector in a 5 Series from a non-US market. Preliminary data showed that the subject vehicle had received the previous remedy, which is why BMW hypothesized an improper repair.
 In June 2025, a US-market 3 Series that also received the earlier remedy developed smoldering at the subject connector. Laboratory work supported the possibility of an improper repair, but nevertheless, BMW decided to broaden its investigation. A January 2026 review of field data identified additional cases of overheating and thermal overload after the 24V608 remedy.
 BMW naturally collected water pumps that showed signs of damage, and the supplier joined the party in February 2026. Pierburg Pump Technology GmbH is the supplier in question, which identified possible leak paths around the electrical connector in March 2026. This, in turn, prompted both parties to turn their attention to the electrical connector's PBT material.
 Photo: BMW 
Testing found severe embrittlement of the polybutylene terephthalate material, but alas, no root cause had been established. Further tests in April 2026 found that embrittlement affected specific areas of the connector, while in-depth analyses confirmed some cracks for good measure. An outside expert was brought in back in May 2026, with all three parties considering hydrolysis of the PBT as a possible explanation.
 In this context, hydrolysis stands for the chemical breakdown of the polyester polymer in the connector. Even a tiny fraction of hydrolysis can compromise the material, turning the plastic brittle. So far, BMW is aware of 10 incidents in the US market involving vehicles repaired under the previous recall.
 The vehicle population includes older Bimmers, including the 2012 through 2016 model year Z4. Affected nameplates further include the 3 Series, 4 Series, and 5 Series, X1, X3, X4, and X5, plus the 2 Series Coupe and Convertible. The largest groups are the 3 Series and X3, totaling 236,702 and 163,727 units, respectively.
 Curiously enough, BMW has not finished developing the new remedy. Once it becomes available, dealers nationwide will carry out the repair at no charge to affected customers. And once said remedy becomes available, customers who paid for related work may qualify for reimbursement as long as they provide adequate proof of payment.
 Dealers have already been notified of 26V733, but customers will have to wait until December 25, 2026, to receive mailed notifications. Indeed, the recall documentation lists Christmas Day as the interim notification date.
